## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Scholars have highlighted the text's relationships with other canonical collections. K.R. Norman notes that the *Dutiya-agāriyavimānavatthu*, along with the preceding *Agāriyavimānavatthu* (Vv 65) and the *Serissakavimānavatthu* (Vv 84), shares verses that also appear in the *Vidhurapaṇḍitajātaka* [Norman 1983].

Computational text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus indicates 96 shared passages between Vv 66 and 16 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Beyond its expected correspondence with the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, the text shares its most extensive segment reuse with its counterpart, the *Paṭhamaagāriyavimānavatthu* (Vv 65, segments §0.1–6.1), as well as significant verse reuse with other *Vimānavatthu* poems including the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), the *Dutiyakuṇḍalīvimānavatthu* (Vv 73), and the *(Uttara) Pāyāsivimānavatthu* (Vv 74) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language alignments with Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan corpora are reported by DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0506a) (§1.3–5.1 ↔ §3129–3140); Paṭhamaagāriyavimānavatthu (Vv 65) (§0.1–6.1 ↔ §0.1–6.1); Guttilavimānavatthu (Vv 33) (§2.1–3.1 ↔ §5.1–6.1); Dutiyakuṇḍalīvimānavatthu (Vv 73) (§1.4–6.1 ↔ §3.1–7.1); (Uttara) Pāyāsivimānavatthu (Vv 74) (§1.3–4.1 ↔ §1.3–4.1); Phaladāyakavimānavatthu (Vv 67) (§1.4–3.3 ↔ §3.1–4.3); Nandanavimānavatthu (Vv 76) (§0.4–4.1 ↔ §0.4–4.1); Cittalatāvimānavatthu (Vv 75) (§0.4–4.1 ↔ §0.4–4.1)
